headline: Milwaukee's Common Council voted 13-0 on 13 Oct 2026 for a one-year ban on new data centers and expansions while the city writes permanent zoning rules.
score_reason: Fresh, confirmed council vote by a major US city and part of a wider spread of local data center pauses; effect is mostly on smaller urban sites.
importance_line: Milwaukee residents gain time to shape the rules and developers face a year's delay, but the region's large AI campuses, by Microsoft and Vantage, are being built outside the city, so the ban mainly touches smaller urban sites.
summary: Urban Milwaukee reports that the Common Council voted 13-0 on Tuesday 13 Oct for a one-year ban on new or expanded data centers of any size while the city writes permanent rules, though developers can still apply for site-specific zoning changes that need public hearings, and state law allows a six-month extension. Lead sponsor Ald. Marina Dimitrijevic said the council wants to find "the right regulatory rules" on noise, energy, water and air quality, while business groups argued a moratorium could discourage investment, jobs and tax revenue.
notes: Read the full article; Mayor Cavalier Johnson's support is confirmed by a spokesperson in the article.
